related_resources.reason: Artist biography, paragraphs about the 1957 Call-and-Response collection, participation and leader-child exchange; the page documents this practice, not a general cross-cultural theory.
Smithsonian Folkways article, bomba and plena paragraphs; notes sung call-and-response, dancer–drummer relation, and specific histories.
Smithsonian teaching resource, section "Through call and response" and Extension 3 on improvisation; a specific teaching/pedagogical account.
William E. Caplin (1998), Oxford, ch. 3 Sentence, pp. 35–48. Public metadata/abstract; full chapter may need access. Period details corroborated using Open Music Theory.
Sections Antecedent phrase and Consequent phrase; weaker cadence then stronger PAC in the discussed Classical theme type.
Sections Presentation phrase, Continuation phrase, Phrase length; example(s) and possible expansions, style-specific criteria.
Reference sections Initiating Functions: Presentation/Antecedent; Medial Functions: Continuation; techniques fragmentation, liquidation, sequential repetition and rhythmic acceleration.
Central-action zone and sequence/fragmentation discussion; explicitly repertoire- and form-specific.
Elizabeth Hellmuth Margulis, Oxford University Press, published online Dec 2013, print 2014; book abstract and contents open. Full book access may be restricted.
Elizabeth Hellmuth Margulis, On Repeat (Oxford), chapter 3, pp. 55–74; public abstract describes cognition and attention, not effects of this invented ostinato.
Steve Reich, essay written 1968, in Writings on Music 1965–2000, Oxford 2004, pp. 34–36; primary statement of Reich aesthetics, not a rule for all process composition.
Sections Formal Containers, Module boundaries, Module Structures; style-scoped examples of timbral, dynamic, melodic, and harmonic section markers.
Official Ardour manual, Session > Import, Region List and drag-drop to editor; tool behavior only, not mixing outcome.
Official software reference for reproducible original audio production.
Region audition/looping in the official Ardour manual.
